text:
helen: FYI seeing intermittent tail spikes in eu-central this morning. Not classic GPU busy — more like KV-cache churn + NIC interrupt bursts. cAdvisor shows huge cgroup rx_packets spikes on gpunode-7.

alert-bot: alert: pod_latency_p99 > 450ms for tenant 'search-embed-prod' on gpunode-7 (03:12 UTC)

devon: interesting. NVML looks fine, but /proc/interrupts shows MSI-X spikes pinned to nic1. Could be a network microburst causing GPU kernel page faults and kvcache evictions.

kai: +1. We've seen NIC-induced kvcache thrash before. Any correlation with batch jobs or large-embedding uploads?

helen: correlates with a nightly bulk-ingest (tenant id: search-embed-prod) that streams many medium-sized requests. QPS isn't huge but bursty.

marta: two questions: 1) short-term mitigation so front-ends don't SRE-page, 2) long-term prevention for multi-tenant safety.

ash: short-term: we can apply an eBPF qdisc bound to that tenant's pod cgroup to smooth NIC bursts and reduce RX interrupt coalescing. That prevents bursts hitting kernel and causing kvcache churn.

devon: we can implement 'soft-fence' logic: detect kvcache miss-rate > threshold and install eBPF shaping + set node-local 'no-new-alloc' label for that tenant for 5-10m. Avoid full eviction.

helen: soft-fence sounds less disruptive than eviction. Does it protect shared GPU KV caches?

ash: it reduces the input burst so less eviction pressure. Not perfect for long-running memory pressure but buys time. For full isolation you'd need dedicated slice or pinned MIG instance.

kai: how about combining with lightweight admission gate that enforces per-tenant pacing at proxy layer? Doing both reduces need for dedicated capacity most of the time.

marta: list of actions I propose: 1) implement eBPF shaping prototype (devon/ash), 2) add kvcache-miss metric per-tenant to infra-metrics (helen), 3) proxy pacing fallback (kai), 4) playbook that triggers dedicated carve for repeat offenders.

devon: prototype notes: run daemonset that subscribes to perf + NV counters, and watchers for /proc/interrupts. On threshold, call infra-control: ```POST /v1/tenants/{id}/soft-fence {"duration_s":600, "shaping_profile":"burst-200ms"}``` then apply tc-bpf on node. Telemetry emitted to infra-metrics as "tenant.soft_fence".

ash: make sure shaping can be applied per-pod without host-wide collateral. Use cgroup clsact + eBPF classifier. I'll open a draft with code snippets.

helen: metric requirements: per-tenant kvcache_miss_rate, per-tenant rx_burst_count, p99 latency, plus node-level interrupt rates. Add tags: tenant_id, node, az.

kai: cost modeling: if soft-fence reduces incidents by 70%, we delay needing dedicated slices. Estimate $Y/hr per slice vs engineering ops cost. I'll run numbers before tomorrow sync.

oom-bot: note: pod search-embed-prod-5 restarted due to OOM at 03:08 UTC (likely memory eviction cascade).

marta: OOMs make this trickier. Soft-fence helps bursts but not steady memory abuse. For repeated OOMs we should trigger automatic migration to preemptible pinned slice and bill tenant if they exceed baseline.

devon: migration path: snapshot pod config -> schedule on preemptible dedicated slice -> annotate tenant with charge_tag. Keep migration fast (<2m).

marta: who volunteers for prototype? devon+ash on eBPF, helen on metrics, kai on proxy pacing, I'll draft runbook and cost thresholds.

devon: I'll spin up a branch and test harness in eu-central non-prod. Will add safety kill-switch to revert shaping if it causes regressions.

helen: adding grafana panels under /dash/infra/kv-noise to track during tests.

kai: schedule 20min sync 09:30 UTC tomorrow to review pilot telemetry and cost calc.

alert-bot: resolved: p99 latency returned to baseline after applying temporary soft-fence at 03:15 UTC.
